ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an aniline fragment in which a benzene ring is connected to NH2; on the right side is a substituted alkene/ester structure, containing an EtO2C substituent, a carbonyl ester fragment bearing OEt, a lower OEt substituent, and a central C=C connection. The curved arrows in the figure only indicate electron movement and, according to the problem statement, are not counted in the number of bonds; all bonds involving hydrogen are also not counted. Reasoning: Count by fragments. In the left aniline fragment, the benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, and the C-N bond from the benzene ring to NH2 has 1 bond, for a total of 7 non-hydrogen bonds. In the right structure, the EtO2C ester fragment, after expansion, has 5 non-hydrogen bonds including the bond connected to the central carbon; the carbonyl ester OEt fragment drawn at the upper right likewise has 5 non-hydrogen bonds including the bond connected to the central carbon; the lower OEt substituent has 3 non-hydrogen bonds; the central C=C connection counts as 1 bond. Therefore the right side has a total of 5+5+3+1=14 non-hydrogen bonds. Adding the two parts gives 7+14=21.

method.method_draft: Count by fragments. For the left aniline component, count 6 C-C bonds in the benzene ring plus 1 C-N bond to NH2, giving 7. For the right component, expand the abbreviations: the EtO2C ester contributes 5 non-H bonds including its attachment to the central carbon; the drawn carbonyl ester with OEt contributes another 5 including its attachment; the lower OEt substituent contributes 3; and the central C=C link contributes 1. Add right-side bonds: 5+5+3+1=14. Add both components: 7+14=21.

method.method_draft: Create a heavy-atom degree table. For the aniline part, the benzene ring has 6 ring edges and one C-N edge, equivalent to 14 heavy-atom bond endpoints, so 7 bonds. For the right structure, list endpoints after expanding groups: central alkene C degree 3, other alkene C degree 2; each ester unit has endpoint sum 9, so two esters give 18; the lower OEt group has endpoint sum 5. The right-side endpoint sum is 3+2+18+5=28, giving 28/2=14 bonds. Combine with the left part: 7+14=21.
method.CoT_raw:
先看图像：左侧是一个苯环连着 NH2 的苯胺片段；右侧是一个忽略箭头后的过渡态片段，包含一个烯烃骨架、两个酯基（左上的 EtO2C 和右上的 C(=O)OEt）以及一个下方的 OEt 取代基。
再按重原子键数计算，且双键、三键都按“一条键”计，不把与氢有关的键算入。
1) 左侧苯胺部分：苯环 6 条环边 + 1 条 C-N 键 = 7 条键。
2) 右侧部分用重原子端点法：上方烯烃碳的度数为 3，另一烯烃碳的度数为 2；每个酯基展开后重原子端点和为 9，两个酯基共 18；下方 OEt 基团端点和为 5。于是右侧端点和 = 3 + 2 + 18 + 5 = 28，对应键数 = 28 / 2 = 14。
3) 总键数 = 7 + 14 = 21。
因此答案是 21。
